newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl says "no ifs and buts" on EMU criteria.
newsitem.headline: Kohl says "no ifs and buts" on EMU criteria.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Friday that countries which want to join European Economic and Monetary Union in 1999 must demonstrate that they can meet the Maastricht criteria long-term and without excuses.
Kohl told around 800 bankers at the European Banking Congress in Frankfurt, "The Maastricht criteria must be met without ifs and buts, and that means in the long term."

Countries which wish to join EMU in the first round must meet economic goals laid down in the Maastricht Treaty in 1997, the year which will form the basis for decisions on who qualifies for entry to the single currency.

Kohl said Europe would stick by its stated goal of basing the decision on who made the grade for EMU on the basis of actual 1997 data -- meaning that estimates, forecasts and goals would not be taken into account.
"By then everyone should have swept his own doorstep and should refrain from pointing out others' failings," he said.
